[[Jawi script|Jawi]] }} '''Yakan''' is an [[Austronesian language]] primarily spoken in [[Basilan]] in the Philippines. It is the native language of the [[Yakan people]], the indigenous as well as the largest ethnic group on the island. It has a total of 110,000 native speakers. Despite being located in the Philippines, it is not closely related to other languages of the country. It is a member of the [[Sama-Bajaw languages]], which in turn are related to the [[Barito languages#Greater Barito|Barito languages]] spoken in southern [[Borneo]], [[Madagascar]] and [[Mayotte]]. ==Phonology== ===Vowels=== Yakan has a simple five-vowel system: {{IPA|[a]}}, {{IPA|[e]}}, {{IPA|[i]}}, {{IPA|[o]}}, {{IPA|[u]}}, with phonemic vowel length: {{Grapheme|ā}} {{IPA|[aː]}}, {{Grapheme|ē}} {{IPA|[eː]}}, {{Grapheme|ī}} {{IPA|[iː]}}, {{Grapheme|ō}} {{IPA|[oː]}}, {{Grapheme|ū}} {{IPA|[uː]}}.{{sfn|Brainard|Behrens|2002|pp=5–6}} ===Consonants=== The following chart lists the consonant phonemes of Yakan.{{sfn|Brainard|Behrens|2002|p=5}} {|class="wikitable" style=text-align:center |- ! colspan=2| !
